descripcion_geo: Mesopotamian city (possibly Sippar on the Euphrates) whose inhabitants were deported to Samaria by the Assyrians.
importancia_estrategica: Source of foreign settlers transplanted to Samaria after the Israeli deportation.

historias.descripcion: After deporting the northern Israelites, the Assyrians bring people from Sepharvaim and other cities to repopulate Samaria.

historias.titulo: The gods of Sepharvaim: Adramelech and Anamelech
historias.descripcion: The Sepharvaim worshiped Adramelech and Anamelech, gods to whom they sacrificed their children in fire.

historias.titulo: Sennacherib: where are the gods of Sepharvaim?
historias.descripcion: The Assyrian general Rabshakeh asks the people of Jerusalem: 'Did the gods of Sepharvaim free their city from my hands?'

personajes.descripcion: He deported Israelites to Assyria and brought Sepharvaim to Samaria.
He used the fall of Sepharvaim as an argument to intimidate Jerusalem.
He responded to Rabshakeh's argument with faith in the God of Israel in the face of the challenge of the gods of Sepharvaim.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Sepharvaim: relevant geographic region in the Old Testament.

mitos.nombre: The gods of Sepharvaim against the God of Israel

judaismo.descripcion: The gods of Sepharvaim could not save their city from Assyria; The contrast with the God of Israel who did save Jerusalem is the central argument of Isaiah's book.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The gods of Sepharvaim could not save their city from Assyria; The contrast with the God of Israel who did save Jerusalem is the central argument of Isaiah's book.
